recipes.name: Birria Tacos
recipes.description: No-marinate slow-cooker beef tacos with browned chuck, chipotle, warm spices, melted cheese and rich dipping sauce. Measure note: original liquid tablespoon amounts are retained; their mL size is not yet confirmed.

ingredients.name: Oaxaca, mozzarella or Monterey Jack cheese

steps:
Prepare the braise.
• Use fully thawed beef. Cut it into large, similar-sized chunks and season with the listed salt and black pepper.
• Chop the brown onion, garlic, Roma tomatoes and chipotle chillies. Zest and juice the orange.
• Measure the spices, stock, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and vinegar. Reserve half the vinegar separately to adjust the cooked sauce.

Brown the beef.
• Heat the cooking oil in a heavy frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches, leaving room between pieces; it will finish cooking in the slow cooker.
• Transfer each batch to the cooker.
• Use a splash of the measured stock to loosen the browned bits from the pan, and add this liquid to the cooker.

Fill the slow cooker.
• Add the chopped brown onion, garlic, tomatoes and chipotle, tomato paste, remaining stock, orange zest and juice, half the vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, oregano, cumin, ground coriander, paprika, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, brown sugar and bay leaves.
• Stir gently. Follow your cooker’s fill limits, usually half to two-thirds full; split the batch if necessary.

Cook until tender.
• Cover and cook on LOW for about 8–10 hours or HIGH for about 5–6 hours.
• Begin checking at the earlier time. The beef should pull apart easily with two forks; if it resists, replace the lid and continue cooking.
• Keep the lid closed between checks. The time is a guide, not a guarantee.

Prepare the toppings.
• Near the end of cooking, grate or shred the cheese. Finely chop the white or red onion and fresh coriander, and cut the limes into wedges.
• Warm the tortillas briefly if they need softening to fold without cracking.

Shred and balance the filling.
• Lift the cooked beef onto a clean tray. Remove and discard all bay leaves from the sauce, then shred the beef.
• Skim some surface fat into a shallow dish for frying the tacos.
• Taste the cooked broth before adding any reserved vinegar. Add it little by little only if needed, allowing for the lime at the table.
• Mix enough broth into the beef to moisten it and keep the rest hot for dipping.

Fill and fry in batches.
• Heat a frying pan over medium heat. Lightly coat a tortilla with the skimmed fat and a little broth, then place it in the pan.
• Add a modest layer of cheese and beef to one half, fold over and fry for about 1–2 minutes per side, until crisp and the cheese melts. Do not overfill.
• Repeat, adjusting the heat if the tortillas darken too quickly.

Serve.
• Serve the tacos immediately with the chopped onion, coriander, lime wedges and small bowls of hot broth.
• Refrigerate leftovers in shallow containers within 2 hours; reheat until steaming hot throughout.

recipes.name: Cajun Chicken Alfredo
recipes.description: Blackened chicken thigh in a cream and parmesan sauce over fettuccine. Measure note: original liquid tablespoon amounts are retained; their mL size is not yet confirmed.
steps:
Prepare everything first.
• Finely dice the onion, mince the garlic, finely grate the Parmesan and zest the lemon.
• Wash the spinach.
• Set out the pasta, cream, stock, butter, mustard and Worcestershire sauce. Put a large pot of water on to heat.

Season the chicken and reserve spice.
• Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, oregano, cayenne and white pepper.
• Before touching raw chicken, reserve one-eighth of the blend in a clean bowl for the sauce.
• Toss the chicken with the remaining blend, half the olive oil and a little salt. Keep the other half of the oil for the pan.

Cook the chicken.
• Heat a wide frying pan over medium-high heat and add some of the reserved pan oil.
• Cook the chicken in uncrowded batches, using the remaining oil as needed. Allow roughly 5–6 minutes per side, adjusting for thickness, until the centre of each fillet reaches 74°C.
• Reduce the heat if the spices begin to burn. Transfer to a clean plate and keep any cooked resting juices.

Start the pasta.
• Once the chicken is cooked, lightly salt the boiling pasta water and add the fettuccine. Follow the packet timing and check for al dente.
• Before draining, reserve a jug of pasta water.
• Make the sauce while the pasta cooks. If it finishes first, drain and hold it briefly without rinsing.

Soften the onion.
• Reduce the frying pan to medium-low. If the spice residue is black and bitter, carefully wipe it out.
• Melt the butter, add the onion and cook for about 4–5 minutes until softened.
• Add the garlic and clean reserved spice blend; stir for 30–60 seconds without scorching.

Reduce the stock.
• Add all the chicken stock and scrape up the browned, non-burnt bits.
• Simmer for about 3–4 minutes until slightly reduced.

steps.text:
Gently simmer the cream.
• Stir in the cream, Dijon mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
• Keep at a gentle simmer for about 5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Avoid a hard boil.

steps:
Finish the sauce off the heat.
• Turn off the heat. Stir in the Parmesan gradually, then the spinach until wilted.
• Add a little reserved pasta water if the sauce is too thick.
• Taste before adding more salt; the stock and cheese already contribute salt.

Toss and serve.
• Slice the cooked chicken. Toss the drained pasta, chicken and cooked resting juices through the sauce.
• Loosen with reserved pasta water a little at a time until glossy. Add lemon zest to taste; serve any remaining lemon as wedges.
• Serve immediately. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days. Reheat once until steaming hot, loosening with a little water if needed.

recipes.name: Parmentier de Poisson
recipes.description: Barramundi and salmon in a creamy leek, fennel and herb sauce beneath buttery mashed potato.
steps:
Prepare the ingredients.
• Heat the oven to 200°C conventional or 180°C fan.
• Peel the potatoes and cut them into even pieces about 3 cm across.
• Wash the leek thoroughly, then finely slice it with the shallots and fennel. Chop the dill, parsley and tarragon.
• Zest half the lemon and cut the rest into serving wedges. Separate the eggs; use the yolks for the mash and refrigerate the whites for another use.

Prepare the fish and divide the seasoning.
• Remove any skin and bones from the barramundi and salmon. Cut them into similar bite-sized pieces and keep refrigerated.
• Reserve two-thirds of the butter for the mash and one-third for the sauce.
• Use two-thirds of the salt for the potato water; divide the remaining salt equally between the mash and sauce. Divide the white pepper equally between the mash and sauce.

steps.text:
Cook the potatoes.
• Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water and add the allocated salt.
• Bring to the boil, then simmer for about 18–20 minutes until a knife slides through easily. Start the timer once simmering.
• While they cook, begin the vegetables in the next step.

Soften the vegetables.
• In a wide saucepan, melt the sauce portion of butter with all the olive oil over medium-low heat.
• Add the leek, shallots and fennel. Cook for about 10 minutes, stirring, until softened without browning.
• If the potatoes finish first, drain them and let them steam dry while you finish this step.

steps:
Make the filling sauce.
• Stir the flour into the softened vegetables and cook for 2 minutes.
• Add the milk gradually, stirring until smooth between additions, then stir in the cream. Simmer gently for about 5–6 minutes until thickened.
• Turn off the heat and add the chopped herbs, lemon zest and sauce portions of salt and white pepper.

Make the mash.
• Drain the tender potatoes if you have not already, and let them steam dry for about 2 minutes.
• Mash with the reserved butter. Let cool briefly so they are no longer fiercely steaming.
• Mix in the egg yolks and mash portions of salt and white pepper. Do not taste after adding the raw yolks.

Assemble the pie.
• Fold the chilled fish through the warm vegetable sauce.
• Transfer to a baking dish with room for the filling, mash and some bubbling space; use two dishes if needed. Spread the mash over the top and roughen it with a fork.
• Set the dish on a baking tray to catch drips.

steps.text:
Bake and check the centre.
• Bake for about 25–35 minutes, until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling.
• Check the centre with a thermometer: this assembled fish-and-egg casserole should reach 74°C. Continue baking if needed.
• Cover the top loosely if it browns too quickly.

Rest and serve.
• Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with the lemon wedges.
• Refrigerate leftovers in shallow containers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot throughout.

recipes.name: Beef Lasagne
recipes.description: Bolognese and bechamel under mozzarella and parmesan. Better on day two. Measure note: original liquid tablespoon amounts are retained; their mL size is not yet confirmed.
steps:
Prepare.
• Dice the onions, mince the garlic and grate the Parmesan.
• Check whether the lasagne sheets need precooking, and follow their packet instructions if they do.
• Set out the remaining ingredients and choose a deep baking dish large enough for the batch, or divide it between two dishes.

Brown the mince in batches.
• Heat a large, heavy pot over medium-high heat. Use half the olive oil to brown the beef in uncrowded batches, breaking up lumps; transfer each batch to a bowl.
• Lower the heat, add the remaining oil and soften the onions for about 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
• Return the beef and its juices to the pot.

steps.text:
Simmer the meat sauce.
• Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes. Add the crushed tomatoes, oregano and basil.
• Simmer gently for about 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rich but still spreadable. Add a little water if it becomes dry.
• Check that the mince is cooked through to 71°C before tasting and adjusting the salt.

steps:
Make the white sauce.
• While the meat sauce simmers, melt the butter in a separate saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes.
• Gradually whisk in the milk, making the mixture smooth between additions.
• Simmer gently, whisking, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Season lightly with salt and a little nutmeg, then take off the heat.

Layer the lasagne.
• Heat the oven to 180°C conventional or 160°C fan. Spread a thin layer of meat sauce over the base of the dish.
• Layer the lasagne sheets with meat sauce, white sauce and mozzarella, reserving enough white sauce and mozzarella for the top. Keep every sheet covered with sauce and follow any packet guidance on sauce depth.
• Finish with the reserved white sauce, mozzarella and all the Parmesan.

steps.text:
Bake covered.
• Cover the dish with foil, keeping it clear of the cheese where possible. Bake for 30 minutes. This is the first check, not the end of cooking.

Uncover and finish baking.
• Remove the foil and bake for about 15–20 minutes more, until browned and bubbling.
• Check that a knife passes easily through the pasta and the centre reaches 74°C. If the pasta is still firm, cover again and continue cooking; add a little hot water around dry edges if needed.

Rest, then portion.
• Rest for 15 minutes before slicing so the layers can settle.
• Refrigerate leftovers in shallow portions within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.
• Reheat once until steaming hot throughout.

recipes.name: Creamy Tuscan Salmon
recipes.description: Seared salmon in a garlic cream sauce with sundried tomato and spinach, roast baby potatoes. Measure note: original liquid tablespoon amounts are retained; their mL size is not yet confirmed.
steps:
Prepare.
• Heat the oven to 200°C conventional or 180°C fan.
• Halve the baby potatoes, cutting any large ones again for even pieces.
• Mince the garlic, drain and chop the sundried tomatoes, grate the Parmesan and wash the spinach.
• Pat the salmon dry and check for pin bones.

steps.text:
Start the potatoes.
• Toss the potatoes with half the listed olive oil, half the salt, half the paprika and all the oregano.
• Spread cut-side down on a baking tray without crowding. Roast for about 30–40 minutes, until golden and tender when pierced.
• Start checking at 30 minutes; begin the salmon when the potatoes have about 15–20 minutes left.

steps:
Cook the salmon.
• Season the salmon with the remaining salt and paprika. Heat the remaining olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat.
• Add the salmon skin-side down, if it has skin, and cook for about 4–6 minutes. Turn and cook the other side, lowering the heat as needed, until the thickest centre reaches 63°C. Thickness affects the timing.
• Transfer to a clean plate.

Soften the aromatics.
• Reduce the pan to medium-low and melt the butter.
• Add the garlic, sundried tomatoes and chilli flakes. Stir for about 1 minute until fragrant, without browning the garlic.

steps.text:
Gently simmer the cream.
• Add the cream and simmer gently for about 5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened.
• Avoid a hard boil.

steps:
Finish the sauce.
• Turn off the heat. Stir in the Parmesan and spinach until the cheese melts and the spinach wilts.
• Taste before adding any extra seasoning.
• Return the cooked salmon to the sauce, skin-side up if applicable, just long enough to warm it through without overcooking.

Check and serve.
• Check that the potatoes are tender all the way through.
• Divide the salmon, sauce and potatoes between portions and serve immediately.
• Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.

recipes.name: Easy Char Siu Chicken
recipes.description: Serves 6–7; 1.1 kg chicken. Prep about 10 minutes plus at least 30 minutes marinating; cooking about 20–25 minutes. App display: 6 servings and 25 minutes. Original measures use 15 mL tablespoons; retains 50–75 mL chicken stock at the final stage.

ingredients.name: Red food colouring (optional; a few drops)

steps:
Make the Char Siu marinade.
• In a large bowl, combine the soy sauce, hoisin sauce, honey, finely minced garlic, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil, Chinese five spice, MSG and 110 mL water.
• Add a few drops of red food colouring if desired, then mix thoroughly.

Marinate the chicken.
• Add the chicken thighs and toss until every piece is coated.
• Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or overnight for a stronger flavour.

Remove the chicken.
• Lift the thighs from the bowl, letting excess marinade drip back in.
• Keep all remaining marinade for the glaze.

Sear the chicken.
• Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat with a little cooking oil.
• Sear the thighs without crowding the pan; 1.1 kg will likely need two batches. Cook the first side for about 3–4 minutes without moving it much, until browned and starting to caramelise, then briefly brown the other side.
• Transfer each batch to a clean plate while searing the rest.

Add the marinade and stock.
• Return one batch of chicken to the pan. Divide the remaining marinade and 50–75 mL stock between batches; use closer to 50 mL if there is already plenty of liquid.
• Bring that batch of sauce to a full bubbling boil because the marinade touched raw chicken. Repeat with the remaining batch, if cooking in two batches.

Finish cooking.
• Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover and cook each batch for about 8–10 minutes, turning the thighs occasionally.
• If the pan cannot comfortably hold all the chicken, cook in two batches with the divided marinade and stock.

Turn it into a sticky glaze.
• When the chicken is nearly cooked, remove the lid and reduce the sauce.
• Turn the thighs through the thickening sauce until a dark, glossy glaze clings. Keep the heat controlled so the honey does not burn.

Check the chicken and serve.
• Check that the thickest part reaches at least 74°C. Remove from the heat and rest for a few minutes.
• Slice the thighs and spoon the thickened glaze over them. Serve with steamed rice and greens; sesame seeds and sliced spring onion are optional finishes.
• Reminder: sear the chicken, add the leftover marinade and 50–75 mL stock, bring to a boil, cover and cook, then uncover and reduce to a sticky glaze.
